Abscond

ab-SKOND · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To abscond to leave secretly, especially to avoid detection or arrest.

The suspect absconded across the border before the warrant was even signed.

Worked Example

Investigators discovered the accountant had absconded with nearly a decade of company funds.

This wasn't an ordinary resignation -- it was a secret, planned escape meant to avoid getting caught, which is exactly abscond.

How Strong Is It? — leave → vanish → abscond

leave vs. abscond

leave vs. abscond: Leaving is a plain, ordinary departure; absconding is secretive and specifically meant to dodge detection or punishment.

vanish vs. abscond

vanish vs. abscond: Absconding implies a person intentionally fled somewhere; vanishing suggests they disappeared without any trace of where they went.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Abscond comes from Latin abs- ('away') + condere ('to hide, put away') -- literally 'to hide oneself away.'

Use the root in a new word: recondite

Use the root in a new word: recondite: Swap the abs- ('away') for re- and the same hiding verb condere gives recondite -- knowledge so tucked away that only specialists ever reach it. One root, two kinds of hiding: a person slipping out of sight, and facts buried out of reach.

Word Choice
